source: Peterson, G. E., & Barney, H. L. (1952). Control methods used in a study of the vowels. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 24(2), 175-184. Table II: mean fundamental and formant frequencies.
note: Adult male (33 speakers) and adult female (28 speakers) MEAN formant frequencies. Children's means are omitted: the benchmark separates two adult populations, and a third population with a different tract length would change what d' is measuring. P&B published F1-F3 only, so F4 is absent throughout - which is exactly the F4-unavailable operating point Phase 1 must not regress on.
benchmarkVowelSetRationale: The seven vowels tabulated in RESONANCE_REDESIGN.md §1.1. This set reproduces the two figures the redesign's acceptance criteria are stated against - v1 d' = 0.85 and a 73-point across-vowel swing - so v2 is measured on the same ruler v1 was. The full ten-vowel set is asserted alongside it so the result cannot be an artefact of the subset.
